corrected_value.title: Cluster Headache is Associated With the Alcohol Dehydrogenase 4 ( ADH4 ) Gene
corrected_value.authors: Rainero; Rubino; Gallone; Fenoglio; Negro; De Martino; Savi; Pinessi

decisions.quote: Genotypic and allelic analyses of the investigated ADH4 polymorphisms rs1126671 and rs1800759 in CH patients suggest that there is no association between these genetic variants and CH in Sweden. The power of this study is much higher compared with previous studies where an association between ADH4 and CH has been found. 16 , 17
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding (target_index 0) correctly identify Reference 16 (Rainero et al., 2010, doi: 10.1111/j.1526-4610.2009.01569.x) as an original Italian case-control study reporting an association between ADH4 variants (rs1126671 and rs1800759) and cluster headache that this paper directly re-tests in a Swedish case-control cohort.

decisions.quote: The data did not support an association of the ADH4 SNPs rs1126671 and rs1800759 with CH. A comparison with previous studies revealed variance in genotype, allele, and haplotype frequencies among the different populations which might contribute to the contradictory results.
decisions.reason: Relative to the resolved original study (Rainero et al., 2010, Reference 16), which reported significant associations between ADH4 SNPs rs1126671 and rs1800759 and cluster headache, the authors state an overall negative replication verdict finding no significant genotype, allele, or haplotype association for either SNP with cluster headache in the Swedish cohort.

decisions.quote: The data on the two ADH4 SNPs for all 779 individuals were exclusively collected for this replication study.
decisions.reason: The study collected new genotype data from an independent sample of 390 Swedish cluster headache patients and 389 controls to re-test previously published associations between ADH4 polymorphisms (rs1126671 and rs1800759) and cluster headache (Rainero et al., 2010).

corrected_value.authors: Zarrilli F, Tomaiuolo R, Ceglia C, et al.
corrected_value.title: Molecular analysis of cluster headache

decisions.quote: The single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs1126671 located in exon 7 of the ADH4 gene was associated with an increased risk for CH in two Italian studies, whereas rs1800759 located in the promoter region of ADH4 could only be associated with CH in the smaller case–control study. 17
decisions.reason: Fourier et al. (2016) empirically retest the genetic association of two ADH4 SNPs (rs1126671 and rs1800759) with cluster headache (CH) in a Swedish case–control cohort (390 cases, 389 controls). While both cited Italian studies reported an association for rs1126671, only reference 17—Zarrilli et al. (2015, 10.1097/AJP.0000000000000075), the smaller Italian case–control study (54 CH patients)—found an association between rs1800759 and CH, and the authors explicitly test both SNPs and compare their genotype and allele frequencies to both Italian studies in the Results and Discussion. The only shipped row (input_row_index 2498) is Rainero et al. (2010, 10.1111/j.1526-4610.2009.01569.x, Reference 16), an independent earlier study of 110 CH patients by a different Italian research group; report equivalence does not apply. No prior adjudication/state files exist at the listed paths.
